Introduce the upstream dataset and link its canonical Hugging Face dataset page.
Keep the dataset's identity independent of a particular model or training recipe.

## Task

Name the upstream task and explain what a model learns or predicts from this data.
For a companion corpus, explain its role rather than inventing a supervised target.

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Input | What is given to the model? |
| Target | What should the model predict, generate, or retrieve? |
| Modality | Text, image, audio, or a combination. |
| Language | Verified upstream language metadata, if available. |
| License Metadata | Publisher-declared metadata; preserve qualifications and source-specific terms. |

## Example Record

Label this as a **synthetic example**. Use invented values in the verified Hub
schema, retaining meaningful types and nesting. State that illustrative media
paths stand in for binary data. Do not silently present an AutoModel-transformed
record as the raw Hub format.

```json
{
  "SOURCE_FIELD": "Invented value demonstrating the task."
}
```

## Schema and Splits

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SOURCE_FIELD` | string | What this field represents in the task. |

| Configuration | Split or Source | Rows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verified Hub configuration | Verified split or source filename | Verified count, or a dash |

Identify the illustrated configuration if the Hub repository has several schemas.
Cite revision-pinned source metadata, or date viewer metadata when it is the source
of counts. Keep upstream splits separate from local training slices and mixtures.

## Use with NeMo AutoModel

| Workflow | Example Setup | Recipe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recipe-backed workflow | Model and relevant data requirements | Link to the exact checked-in YAML. |

Link the adapter and explain any required preparation, field conversion, mixture
membership, or validation overlap. Recipe existence does not establish benchmark
results. Keep launch instructions in the linked recipe or guide.
